# Get-ZbxToken

## SYNOPSIS

Gets the API tokens that log users in to the API.

## SYNTAX

### All (Default)

```
Get-ZbxToken [-Limit <int>] [-SortField <string[]>] [-Id <ulong[]>] [-User <ZabbixReference<ZabbixUser>[]>] [-InputObject <PSObject>] [-SortOrder <ZabbixSortOrder[]>] [-Search <Hashtable>] [-SearchByAny] [-StartSearch] [-ExcludeSearch] [-SearchWildcardsEnabled] [-CountOutput] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-First <UInt64>] [-Skip <UInt64>] [-IncludeTotalCount] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### ByName

```
Get-ZbxToken [-Name] <string[]> [-Limit <int>] [-SortField <string[]>] [-User <ZabbixReference<ZabbixUser>[]>] [-InputObject <PSObject>] [-SortOrder <ZabbixSortOrder[]>] [-Search <Hashtable>] [-SearchByAny] [-StartSearch] [-ExcludeSearch] [-SearchWildcardsEnabled] [-CountOutput] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-First <UInt64>] [-Skip <UInt64>] [-IncludeTotalCount] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### ById

```
Get-ZbxToken [-SortField <string[]>] -Id <ulong[]> [-User <ZabbixReference<ZabbixUser>[]>] [-InputObject <PSObject>] [-SortOrder <ZabbixSortOrder[]>] [-Search <Hashtable>] [-SearchByAny] [-StartSearch] [-ExcludeSearch] [-SearchWildcardsEnabled] [-CountOutput] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-First <UInt64>] [-Skip <UInt64>] [-IncludeTotalCount] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### ByFilter

```
Get-ZbxToken [-SortField <string[]>] -Filter <ZabbixTokenGetParameters> [-User <ZabbixReference<ZabbixUser>[]>] [-InputObject <PSObject>] [-SortOrder <ZabbixSortOrder[]>] [-Search <Hashtable>] [-SearchByAny] [-StartSearch] [-ExcludeSearch] [-SearchWildcardsEnabled] [-CountOutput] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-First <UInt64>] [-Skip <UInt64>] [-IncludeTotalCount] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

An API token logs a user in to the API without a password; it is created without its secret, which the server generates once (token.generate). The Get-ZbxToken cmdlet reads them with token.get: all of them up to -Limit, by name with -Name (* and ? are wildcards), by id with -Id or from the pipeline, or with the whole token.get selection in -Filter. -User narrows the result to the API tokens of the given users, each a name, an id or a piped object. It writes ZabbixToken objects or, with -CountOutput, the number of matches; it needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Get an API token by name

```powershell
Get-ZbxToken -Name 'Inventory script'
```

Gets the API token named Inventory script. A * or ? in -Name makes it a search, so -Name 'Inventory*' gets every API token whose name starts with Inventory.

### Example 2: Get the API tokens of a user

```powershell
Get-ZbxToken -User 'jdoe'
```

Gets the API tokens of the user jdoe. -User takes a name, an id or an object; a user piped from Get-ZbxUser binds to it by its UserId property.

### Example 3: Search API tokens with a filter

```powershell
Get-ZbxToken -Filter @{ search = @{ name = 'Inventory' }; limit = 10 }
```

-Filter takes the whole token.get selection, keyed by the API's field names: here at most ten API tokens whose name contains Inventory.

## INPUTS

- `ulong[]`: Bound to -Id (ByPropertyName).
- `ZabbixReference<ZabbixUser>[]`: Bound to -User (ByPropertyName). Represents a reference to an API object: a parameter that points at an API object takes its id, its name, or the object itself piped from a Get- cmdlet, and becomes an id before the call — one parameter, three spellings, one resolution.
- `PSObject`: Bound to -InputObject (ByValue). Each object as the API answers it.

## OUTPUTS

- `ZabbixToken`: Token class.
